records.reason: This error vocabulary reports decode failures; it does not decide whether a type-signals document may be reused or compare the complete AC-04 cache identity. Reuse and fingerprint behavior is covered by the reuse and fingerprint entries, so AC-04 is not entry-local behavior.

This domain construction seam only hashes and decodes one caller-provided byte slice. It does not decide type-signal reuse or create the complete cache identity required by IN-03, so that reuse/fingerprint promise is not behavior of this entry.

This domain construction seam has no cache lookup, worktree observation, Cargo-input discovery, or reuse decision; it only builds a typed value from supplied bytes. The complete reuse and authoritative-fingerprint promise in AC-04 is not behavior of this entry.

This function has no output path, target directory, lock handle, writer coordination, or generation observation. It only hashes and decodes bytes already supplied by its caller, so IN-07's lock-held path-to-snapshot and ABA guarantee is not entry-local behavior.

This byte-value factory neither resolves an expected rustdoc path nor acquires a target-directory lock or compares input generations before output. CO-07's lock-scoped output capture is therefore not behavior of this entry.

This function receives bytes after I/O and has no lock, exporter, target-directory ownership, writer-participation check, or fingerprint recheck. AC-06's end-to-end export and ABA safety conditions are not observable behavior of this byte-construction entry.

This domain constructor accepts an already resolved execution identity and byte slice and creates a typed snapshot. It does not decide cache reuse or discover the authoritative implementation and resolution inputs required by IN-03.

This constructor has no cache lookup, worktree check, Cargo-input discovery, or reuse decision; its inputs are already supplied. The complete AC-04 reuse and authoritative-fingerprint gate is not behavior of this entry.

This constructor does not acquire or retain a trusted-root lock, resolve an output path, coordinate writers, or observe generations; it only packages caller-supplied identity, hash, and decoded bytes. IN-07's lock-scoped capture and ABA guarantee is not entry-local behavior.

This domain factory does not determine or read an expected output path and cannot establish target-directory ownership or the pre-write fingerprint comparison described by CO-07. Those conditions are not behavior of this entry.

This constructor has no exporter, target-directory lock, writer-coordination check, or input/resolution recheck. AC-06's end-to-end lock interval and changed-generation rejection are not observable behavior of this entry.
This path value has no lock, exporter, or generation observation, so lock-held snapshot and ABA guarantees are not its behavior.
This type neither hashes rustdoc JSON bytes nor holds a target-directory lock.
A confined path value does not acquire an exclusive lock or detect non-cooperating writers.

The ImplementationFingerprint declaration is a digest wrapper that stores an already computed Sha256Digest. It does not discover workspace, environment, PATH-tool, or cargo-metadata inputs and does not bind declaration, resolution, and execution identity into one cache key.

The ImplementationFingerprint declaration stores only an already computed Sha256Digest. It does not walk workspace files, apply exclusions, resolve tools, include cargo-metadata bytes, or produce authoritative-input errors for symlink and limit failures.
The ImplementationFingerprint declaration stores only an already computed Sha256Digest. It does not decide type-signal reuse or construct the complete AC-04 cache key from hermetic inputs.

The ResolutionFingerprint declaration is a digest wrapper that stores an already computed Sha256Digest. It does not assemble the resolution snapshot or implementation-input set, so IN-03's authoritative input discovery is not behavior of this type.
This newtype only stores a resolved Cargo target directory path used as one identity component. It does not compose the complete reuse identity or fingerprint rustdoc graph inputs.
An identity value does not acquire the shared rustdoc output lock or wait 120 seconds.
This type does not exclusively own a target directory or route rustdoc writers through a common lock.
This type has no lock timeout, lock-operation failure path, or retry loop.
Pairing identity components does not implement Unix descriptor-relative no-follow locking.
This identity value does not gate export on Unix trusted-root lock availability.
Construction-error variants do not open lock descriptors or validate trusted roots.
This error type does not encode platform lock support or snapshot-reuse policy.
The TypeSignalsCacheKey declaration stores an already computed identity tuple. It does not capture rustdoc bytes, select an output path, or hold the target-directory lock.
The TypeSignalsCacheKey declaration stores an already computed identity tuple. It does not verify an expected rustdoc output path or hash JSON while a lock is held.
The TypeSignalsCacheKey declaration provides stored-value equality only. It does not own an exclusive lock, check cooperative writers, or detect ABA replacements.
This enum is the reuse outcome vocabulary. Fail-closed fingerprint construction happens before the enum is produced, not as behavior of the enum type itself.

The declaration is an outcome enum with only SkipEvaluation and ReextractAndEvaluate variants. It classifies already-verified cache-key comparisons; worktree observation, fingerprint construction, and fail-closed input acquisition happen before this enum is produced.

This input value carries recorded and current cache keys plus cleanliness/authority flags. It does not determine rustdoc output paths, hold an export lock, or snapshot JSON bytes, so IN-07 lock-held capture is not local behavior of this type.
Constructing a reuse input does not acquire exclusive target-directory ownership, require writer participation, or detect ABA replacements of rustdoc output.
This value object stores one SHA-256 digest and one decoded rustdoc graph produced from caller-supplied bytes. It does not assemble cache identity, walk Cargo inputs, or decide type-signal reuse.
This value object has no cache lookup, worktree observation, or reuse gate. AC-04's complete identity match on a clean worktree is not behavior of the captured-json value.
This value object has no target directory, lock handle, output path, or generation observation. It only retains the hash and graph of bytes already supplied by its constructor.
This value object neither resolves an expected rustdoc path nor holds a lock through output snapshotting. CO-07's lock-scoped capture is not local behavior of the stored hash and graph.
This value object has no exporter, writer-participation check, or fingerprint revalidation. Exclusive target ownership and ABA rejection are not observable on the captured-json type.
This snapshot type has no cache lookup or worktree check. AC-04's complete reuse gate is not behavior of the stored identity-bearing capture.

The snapshot type has no public constructor from independently built identity and captured values, and it does not itself acquire a lock or reread paths. Mixed-generation assembly is excluded from this type's surface rather than detected as I/O ABA.
This snapshot type retains identity and captured bytes after construction. It does not confirm exclusive target ownership or compare start/end fingerprints before persist.
This snapshot type cannot hold a lock, reject non-cooperative writers, or detect ABA of rustdoc output. Those conditions are not local behavior of the stored proof value.
This digest type has no cache, worktree, or reuse decision. AC-04's complete identity match is not behavior of the hash value.
This digest type does not acquire a lock or snapshot JSON from an expected path. It only names the hash of bytes already in memory.
This digest type does not confirm target-directory ownership or hold a lock through output capture. CO-07 is not local behavior of the stored digest.
This digest type cannot lock a target directory, exclude writers, or recheck fingerprints. AC-06 lock and ABA conditions are not observable on the hash value.

This context value carries already captured rustdoc graphs keyed by layer. It has no lock handle, expected output path, or generation observation, so mixed-generation and ABA prevention are not local behavior of the stored context.
This context type does not resolve an expected rustdoc path, acquire a target-directory lock, or snapshot JSON bytes. CO-07's lock-scoped capture is not behavior of the assembled context value.

This context value does not own a target directory, participate in writer locking, or recheck fingerprints before persist. AC-06's exclusive-lock and ABA conditions are not observable on the context type.
This error type does not enumerate architecture layers or enforce the 64-layer export bound. IN-04's layer-limit behavior is not local to the error vocabulary.
This error enum does not iterate configured layers or continue after a 64-layer overflow. CO-05 is not behavior of the error vocabulary.
This error type does not implement the 64-layer ceiling or split-continuation policy. AC-05 is not local behavior of the error vocabulary.
This error enum does not acquire or time out a target-directory lock. IN-05's exclusive-lock serialization is not behavior of the error vocabulary.
This error type has no lock file, writer set, or trusted-root descriptor. CO-06's lock policy is not local to the error vocabulary.
This error enum does not wait on or retry a 120-second lock. AC-07's lock-failure stop is not behavior of the error vocabulary.
This error type does not open descriptor-relative lock files or inspect platform lock capability. IN-06 is not local to the error vocabulary.
This error enum does not implement Unix-only trusted-root admission. AC-08 is not behavior of the error vocabulary.

The declaration docs identify this as "Rustdoc port error vocabulary (AC-04, CO-04)." This error vocabulary does not look up a type-signal cache or inspect worktree cleanliness; the AC-04 reuse slice is owned by decide_type_signals_reuse / execute_type_signals_for_layer and is unused by this error vocabulary.
